sanskrit: īśānahetoḥ pratinirmitāṃ tāṃ; tvaṣṭrā ripūṇām asudehabhakṣām bhūmyantarikṣādijalāśayāni; prasahya bhūtāni nihantum īśām
english: That spear had been forged by Tvaṣṭṛ for Īśāna's sake, a devourer of the lives and bodies of foes, with power to slay by force the beings that dwell in earth, in the sky, in the waters, and elsewhere.

sanskrit: ghaṇṭāpatākāmaṇivajrabhājaṃ; vaiḍūryacitrāṃ tapanīyadaṇḍām tvaṣṭrā prayatnān niyamena kḷptāṃ; brahmadviṣām antakarīm amoghām
english: It was hung with bells and banners, set with gems and adamant, gleaming with cat's-eye, its shaft of refined gold; fashioned by Tvaṣṭṛ with effort and due rite, it was unfailing, the bringer of death to the haters of Brahman.

sanskrit: balaprayatnād adhirūḍhavegāṃ; mantraiś ca ghorair abhimantrayitvā sasarja mārgeṇa ca tāṃ pareṇa; vadhāya madrādhipates tadānīm
english: Charged with momentum by force and effort, hallowed with terrible mantras, he then loosed it along that surpassing course for the slaying of the lord of the Madras.

sanskrit: hato 'sy asāv ity abhigarjamāno; rudro 'ntakāyāntakaraṃ yatheṣum prasārya bāhuṃ sudṛḍhaṃ supāṇiṃ; krodhena nṛtyann iva dharmarājaḥ
english: "You are slain!" the King of Righteousness roared aloud, as Rudra lets fly the death-dealing shaft against Death himself, stretching forth his firm, fair-handed arm, all but dancing in his wrath.

sanskrit: tāṃ sarvaśaktyā prahitāṃ sa śaktiṃ; yudhiṣṭhireṇāprativāryavīryām pratigrahāyābhinanarda śalyaḥ; samyag ghutām agnir ivājyadhārām
english: That spear, hurled by Yudhiṣṭhira with all his might, its force not to be turned aside, Śalya roared out to receive, as fire roars to welcome a stream of butter rightly poured in oblation.

sanskrit: sā tasya marmāṇi vidārya śubhram; uro viśālaṃ ca tathaiva varma viveśa gāṃ toyam ivāprasaktā; yaśo viśālaṃ nṛpater dahantī
english: Cleaving his vital parts and his broad bright chest, and likewise his armor, it sank in as water sinks unhindered into the earth, consuming the king's wide-spread glory.

sanskrit: nāsākṣikarṇāsyaviniḥsṛtena; prasyandatā ca vraṇasaṃbhavena saṃsiktagātro rudhireṇa so 'bhūt; krauñco yathā skandahato mahādriḥ
english: With the blood that streamed from his nose, eyes, ears, and mouth, and that welled forth from the wound, his limbs were drenched—like the great mountain Krauñca smitten by Skanda.

sanskrit: prasārya bāhū sa rathād gato gāṃ; saṃchinnavarmā kurunandanena mahendravāhapratimo mahātmā; vajrāhataṃ śṛṅgam ivācalasya
english: His armor cleft asunder by the joy of the Kurus, the great-souled one, who matched the mount of mighty Indra, flung wide his arms and fell from his chariot to the earth, like the peak of a mountain struck by the thunderbolt.

sanskrit: bāhū prasāryābhimukho dharmarājasya madrarāṭ tato nipatito bhūmāv indradhvaja ivocchritaḥ
english: Stretching out his arms, the king of the Madras, facing the King of Righteousness, then fell to the ground like an upraised banner of Indra.

sanskrit: sa tathā bhinnasarvāṅgo rudhireṇa samukṣitaḥ pratyudgata iva premṇā bhūmyā sa narapuṃgavaḥ
english: With every limb thus rent and bathed in blood, that bull among men seemed as if the earth herself had risen up in love to meet him.

sanskrit: priyayā kāntayā kāntaḥ patamāna ivorasi ciraṃ bhuktvā vasumatīṃ priyāṃ kāntām iva prabhuḥ sarvair aṅgaiḥ samāśliṣya prasupta iva so 'bhavat
english: Like a lover sinking upon the breast of his cherished beloved, having long enjoyed the bountiful earth as a man enjoys his dear and lovely wife, that lord, embracing her with all his limbs, seemed as one fallen asleep.

sanskrit: dharmye dharmātmanā yuddhe nihato dharmasūnunā samyag ghuta iva sviṣṭaḥ praśānto 'gnir ivādhvare
english: Slain in righteous battle by the righteous-souled son of Dharma, he was like a fire well-fed with rightful oblation, grown calm at the close of the sacrifice.

sanskrit: śaktyā vibhinnahṛdayaṃ vipraviddhāyudhadhvajam saṃśāntam api madreśaṃ lakṣmīr naiva vyamuñcata
english: Though his heart was riven by the spear, his weapons and banner cast away, and though the lord of the Madras lay stilled in death, splendor would not forsake him.

sanskrit: tato yudhiṣṭhiraś cāpam ādāyendradhanuṣprabham vyadhamad dviṣataḥ saṃkhye khagarāḍ iva pannagān dehāsūn niśitair bhallai ripūṇāṃ nāśayan kṣaṇāt
english: Then Yudhiṣṭhira, taking up his bow bright as Indra's rainbow, scattered his foes in the fight as the king of birds scatters serpents, in an instant destroying with his keen broad-headed shafts the bodies and the lives of his enemies.

sanskrit: tataḥ pārthasya bāṇaughair āvṛtāḥ sainikās tava nimīlitākṣāḥ kṣiṇvanto bhṛśam anyonyam arditāḥ saṃnyastakavacā dehair vipatrāyudhajīvitāḥ
english: Then your soldiers, enveloped by the floods of the Pārtha's arrows, their eyes shut fast, sorely afflicted, wasting one another grievously, cast off their mail, their bodies stripped of weapons, of armor, and of life.

sanskrit: tataḥ śalye nipatite madrarājānujo yuvā bhrātuḥ sarvair guṇais tulyo rathī pāṇḍavam abhyayāt
english: Then, when Śalya had fallen, the young brother of the Madra king, a charioteer the equal of his brother in every quality, rushed upon the Pāṇḍava.

sanskrit: vivyādha ca naraśreṣṭho nārācair bahubhis tvaran hatasyāpacitiṃ bhrātuś cikīrṣur yuddhadurmadaḥ
english: And that best of men, frenzied with battle, eager to avenge his slain brother, swiftly pierced him with many iron shafts.

sanskrit: taṃ vivyādhāśugaiḥ ṣaḍbhir dharmarājas tvarann iva kārmukaṃ cāsya ciccheda kṣurābhyāṃ dhvajam eva ca
english: The King of Righteousness, moving as if in haste, pierced him with six swift arrows and, with two razor-edged shafts, cut apart his bow and his banner too.

sanskrit: tato 'sya dīpyamānena sudṛḍhena śitena ca pramukhe vartamānasya bhallenāpāharac chiraḥ
english: Then, with a blazing, firm, and whetted broad-headed shaft, he struck off the head of that warrior who stood there before him.

sanskrit: sakuṇḍalaṃ tad dadṛśe patamānaṃ śiro rathāt puṇyakṣayam iva prāpya patantaṃ svargavāsinam
english: That head, still wearing its earrings, was seen to fall from the chariot, like a dweller in heaven plummeting down upon the exhaustion of his merit.

sanskrit: tasyāpakṛṣṭaśīrṣaṃ tac charīraṃ patitaṃ rathāt rudhireṇāvasiktāṅgaṃ dṛṣṭvā sainyam abhajyata
english: Seeing his headless body, fallen from the chariot, its limbs drenched with blood, the army broke and fled.

sanskrit: vicitrakavace tasmin hate madranṛpānuje hāhākāraṃ vikurvāṇāḥ kuravo vipradudruvuḥ
english: When that brother of the Madra king, clad in many-hued armor, was slain, the Kurus, raising cries of woe, scattered in flight.

sanskrit: śalyānujaṃ hataṃ dṛṣṭvā tāvakās tyaktajīvitāḥ vitresuḥ pāṇḍavabhayād rajodhvastās tathā bhṛśam
english: Seeing Śalya's younger brother slain, your men, ready to lay down their lives, covered thickly with dust, trembled exceedingly in their dread of the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: tāṃs tathā bhajyatas trastān kauravān bharatarṣabha śiner naptā kiran bāṇair abhyavartata sātyakiḥ
english: Upon those Kauravas thus broken and terrified, O bull of the Bharatas, Sātyaki, grandson of Śini, advanced, showering them with arrows.

sanskrit: tam āyāntaṃ maheṣvāsam aprasahyaṃ durāsadam hārdikyas tvarito rājan pratyagṛhṇād abhītavat
english: As that mighty bowman came on, irresistible and hard to withstand, Hārdikya, O king, swiftly and without fear received him.

sanskrit: tau sametau mahātmānau vārṣṇeyāv aparājitau hārdikyaḥ sātyakiś caiva siṃhāv iva madotkaṭau
english: Those two great-souled and unconquered scions of the Vṛṣṇis came together, Hārdikya and Sātyaki, like two lions maddened with rut.

sanskrit: iṣubhir vimalābhāsaiś chādayantau parasparam arcirbhir iva sūryasya divākarasamaprabhau
english: With arrows of spotless luster they veiled each other, bright as the sun's own beams, each rivaling the day-maker in radiance.

sanskrit: cāpamārgabaloddhūtān mārgaṇān vṛṣṇisiṃhayoḥ ākāśe samapaśyāma pataṃgān iva śīghragān
english: The shafts of those two Vṛṣṇi lions, sped by the force of their bowstrings' course, we beheld in the sky moving swift as flights of birds.

sanskrit: sātyakiṃ daśabhir viddhvā hayāṃś cāsya tribhiḥ śaraiḥ cāpam ekena ciccheda hārdikyo nataparvaṇā
english: Hārdikya pierced Sātyaki with ten arrows and his horses with three, and with a single keen-jointed shaft cut asunder his bow.

sanskrit: tan nikṛttaṃ dhanuḥ śreṣṭham apāsya śinipuṃgavaḥ anyad ādatta vegena vegavattaram āyudham
english: Casting aside that fine bow now severed, the bull of the Śinis swiftly took up another weapon, mightier still in force.

sanskrit: tad ādāya dhanuḥ śreṣṭhaṃ variṣṭhaḥ sarvadhanvinām hārdikyaṃ daśabhir bāṇaiḥ pratyavidhyat stanāntare
english: Taking up that excellent bow, the foremost of all archers struck Hārdikya in return, full upon the breast, with ten arrows.

sanskrit: tato rathaṃ yugeṣāṃ ca chittvā bhallaiḥ susaṃyataiḥ aśvāṃs tasyāvadhīt tūrṇam ubhau ca pārṣṇisārathī
english: Then, cutting apart his chariot, yoke, and pole with well-aimed broad-headed shafts, he swiftly slew his horses and both his flanking charioteers.

sanskrit: madrarāje hate rājan virathe kṛtavarmaṇi duryodhanabalaṃ sarvaṃ punar āsīt parāṅmukham
english: With the king of the Madras slain, O king, and Kṛtavarman robbed of his chariot, the whole host of Duryodhana once again turned its back in flight.

sanskrit: tatpare nāvabudhyanta sainyena rajasā vṛte balaṃ tu hatabhūyiṣṭhaṃ tat tadāsīt parāṅmukham
english: The enemy did not perceive it, the field being shrouded by the army's dust; yet that force, the greater part of it slain, had then turned away in retreat.

sanskrit: tato muhūrtāt te 'paśyan rajo bhaumaṃ samutthitam vividhaiḥ śoṇitasrāvaiḥ praśāntaṃ puruṣarṣabha
english: Then in a moment they saw the dust that had risen from the earth laid to rest by the manifold streams of blood, O bull among men.

sanskrit: tato duryodhano dṛṣṭvā bhagnaṃ svabalam antikāt javenāpatataḥ pārthān ekaḥ sarvān avārayat
english: Then Duryodhana, seeing his own force shattered close at hand, alone held back all the Pārthas as they swiftly bore down upon him.

sanskrit: pāṇḍavān sarathān dṛṣṭvā dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ ca pārṣatam ānartaṃ ca durādharṣaṃ śitair bāṇair avākirat
english: Seeing the Pāṇḍavas with their chariots, and Dhṛṣṭadyumna son of Pṛṣata, and the unassailable man of Ānarta, he overwhelmed them with whetted arrows.

sanskrit: taṃ pare nābhyavartanta martyā mṛtyum ivāgatam athānyaṃ ratham āsthāya hārdikyo 'pi nyavartata
english: The foe did not close with him, as mortals shun Death come near; and Hārdikya too, mounting another chariot, returned to the fight.

sanskrit: tato yudhiṣṭhiro rājā tvaramāṇo mahārathaḥ caturbhir nijaghānāśvān patribhiḥ kṛtavarmaṇaḥ vivyādha gautamaṃ cāpi ṣaḍbhir bhallaiḥ sutejanaiḥ
english: Then King Yudhiṣṭhira, that great chariot-warrior, in haste slew Kṛtavarman's horses with four feathered shafts, and pierced Gautama too with six keen broad-headed arrows.

sanskrit: aśvatthāmā tato rājñā hatāśvaṃ virathīkṛtam samapovāha hārdikyaṃ svarathena yudhiṣṭhirāt
english: Then Aśvatthāman bore Hārdikya away from Yudhiṣṭhira upon his own chariot, since the king had killed his horses and left him without a car.

sanskrit: tataḥ śāradvato 'ṣṭābhiḥ pratyavidhyad yudhiṣṭhiram vivyādha cāśvān niśitais tasyāṣṭābhiḥ śilīmukhaiḥ
english: Then the son of Śaradvat struck Yudhiṣṭhira in return with eight arrows, and pierced his horses with eight keen shafts.

sanskrit: evam etan mahārāja yuddhaśeṣam avartata tava durmantrite rājan sahaputrasya bhārata
english: Thus it was, O great king, that this remnant of the battle came to pass, through your evil counsel, O Bhārata, yours and your son's together.

sanskrit: tasmin maheṣvāsavare viśaste; saṃgrāmamadhye kurupuṃgavena pārthāḥ sametāḥ paramaprahṛṣṭāḥ; śaṅkhān pradadhmur hatam īkṣya śalyam
english: When that foremost of mighty bowmen had been laid low in the midst of battle by the bull of the Kurus, the Pārthas, gathered together and filled with utmost joy, blew their conches at the sight of Śalya slain.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiraṃ ca praśaśaṃsur ājau; purā surā vṛtravadhe yathendram cakruś ca nānāvidhavādyaśabdān; ninādayanto vasudhāṃ samantāt
english: And they praised Yudhiṣṭhira in the fray as of old the gods praised Indra at the slaying of Vṛtra, and they raised the sounds of instruments of every kind, making the earth resound on every side.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca śalye tu nihate rājan madrarājapadānugāḥ rathāḥ saptaśatā vīrā niryayur mahato balāt
english: Saṃjaya said: When Śalya had been slain, O king, the followers of the Madra king, seven hundred heroic chariot-warriors, sallied forth from the great host.

sanskrit: duryodhanas tu dviradam āruhyācalasaṃnibham chatreṇa dhriyamāṇena vījyamānaś ca cāmaraiḥ na gantavyaṃ na gantavyam iti madrān avārayat
english: But Duryodhana, mounted upon an elephant like a mountain, the parasol held above him and the yak-tail whisks fanning him, restrained the Madras, crying, "You must not go! You must not go!"

sanskrit: duryodhanena te vīrā vāryamāṇāḥ punaḥ punaḥ yudhiṣṭhiraṃ jighāṃsantaḥ pāṇḍūnāṃ prāviśan balam
english: Though held back again and again by Duryodhana, those heroes, longing to slay Yudhiṣṭhira, plunged into the host of the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: te tu śūrā mahārāja kṛtacittāḥ sma yodhane dhanuḥśabdaṃ mahat kṛtvā sahāyudhyanta pāṇḍavaiḥ
english: Those heroes, O great king, their minds resolved upon battle, raising a mighty twang of bowstrings, fought all together against the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: śrutvā tu nihataṃ śalyaṃ dharmaputraṃ ca pīḍitam madrarājapriye yuktair madrakāṇāṃ mahārathaiḥ
english: But hearing that Śalya was slain and that the son of Dharma was hard pressed by the great chariot-warriors of the Madras, who were intent upon their king's pleasure—

sanskrit: ājagāma tataḥ pārtho gāṇḍīvaṃ vikṣipan dhanuḥ pūrayan rathaghoṣeṇa diśaḥ sarvā mahārathaḥ
english: —the Pārtha then came on, drawing his bow Gāṇḍīva, that great chariot-warrior filling all the quarters with the thunder of his car.

sanskrit: tato 'rjunaś ca bhīmaś ca mādrīputrau ca pāṇḍavau sātyakiś ca naravyāghro draupadeyāś ca sarvaśaḥ
english: Then Arjuna and Bhīma, and the two sons of Mādrī, the Pāṇḍavas, and Sātyaki, that tiger among men, and the sons of Draupadī, every one—

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnaḥ śikhaṇḍī ca pāñcālāḥ saha somakaiḥ yudhiṣṭhiraṃ parīpsantaḥ samantāt paryavārayan
english: —Dhṛṣṭadyumna and Śikhaṇḍin, and the Pāñcālas together with the Somakas, seeking to protect Yudhiṣṭhira, ringed him about on every side.

sanskrit: te samantāt parivṛtāḥ pāṇḍavaiḥ puruṣarṣabhāḥ kṣobhayanti sma tāṃ senāṃ makarāḥ sāgaraṃ yathā
english: Those bulls among men, surrounded on all sides by the Pāṇḍavas, set that army churning as sea-monsters churn the ocean.

sanskrit: purovātena gaṅgeva kṣobhyamānā mahānadī akṣobhyata tadā rājan pāṇḍūnāṃ dhvajinī punaḥ
english: Like the great river Gaṅgā lashed into turmoil by a head-on gale, the banner-host of the Pāṇḍavas was once again, O king, thrown into uproar.

sanskrit: praskandya senāṃ mahatīṃ tyaktātmāno mahārathāḥ vṛkṣān iva mahāvātāḥ kampayanti sma tāvakāḥ
english: Storming into that great army, the great chariot-warriors who held their lives as nothing made your men quake as mighty winds shake the trees.

sanskrit: bahavaś cukruśus tatra kva sa rājā yudhiṣṭhiraḥ bhrātaro vāsya te śūrā dṛśyante neha ke cana
english: Many cried out there, "Where is that king Yudhiṣṭhira? Nor are any of his heroic brothers to be seen here at all."

sanskrit: pāñcālānāṃ mahāvīryāḥ śikhaṇḍī ca mahārathaḥ dhṛṣṭadyumno 'tha śaineyo draupadeyāś ca sarvaśaḥ
english: "The mighty warriors of the Pāñcālas, and Śikhaṇḍin that great chariot-fighter, and Dhṛṣṭadyumna, and the grandson of Śini, and the sons of Draupadī, all of them—"

sanskrit: evaṃ tān vādinaḥ śūrān draupadeyā mahārathāḥ abhyaghnan yuyudhānaś ca madrarājapadānugān
english: As they spoke thus, the heroic sons of Draupadī, great chariot-warriors, and Yuyudhāna, smote those followers of the Madra king.

sanskrit: cakrair vimathitaiḥ ke cit ke cic chinnair mahādhvajaiḥ pratyadṛśyanta samare tāvakā nihatāḥ paraiḥ
english: Some with their wheels crushed, some with their tall banners cut down, your men were seen in the battle, slain by the foe.

sanskrit: ālokya pāṇḍavān yuddhe yodhā rājan samantataḥ vāryamāṇā yayur vegāt tava putreṇa bhārata
english: Beholding the Pāṇḍavas in the battle, your warriors, O king, though restrained by your son, rushed forth with violence on every side, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: duryodhanas tu tān vīrān vārayām āsa sāntvayan na cāsya śāsanaṃ kaś cit tatra cakre mahārathaḥ
english: Duryodhana sought to restrain those heroes, soothing them with gentle words, yet not one of those great chariot-warriors there obeyed his command.

sanskrit: tato gāndhārarājasya putraḥ śakunir abravīt duryodhanaṃ mahārāja vacanaṃ vacanakṣamaḥ
english: Then the son of the Gāndhāra king, Śakuni, skilled in speech, spoke these words to Duryodhana, O great king:

sanskrit: kiṃ naḥ saṃprekṣamāṇānāṃ madrāṇāṃ hanyate balam na yuktam etat samare tvayi tiṣṭhati bhārata
english: "Why is the force of the Madras being cut down before our very eyes? This is not fitting, O Bhārata, while you stand fast in the battle.

sanskrit: sahitair nāma yoddhavyam ity eṣa samayaḥ kṛtaḥ atha kasmāt parān eva ghnato marṣayase nṛpa
english: "That we should fight in concert—such a compact was made; then why, O king, do you suffer the foe to go on slaying?"

sanskrit: duryodhana uvāca vāryamāṇā mayā pūrvaṃ naite cakrur vaco mama ete hi nihatāḥ sarve praskannāḥ pāṇḍuvāhinīm
english: Duryodhana said: "Restrained by me before, these men would not heed my word; for all these who have been slain plunged headlong into the host of the Pāṇḍavas."

sanskrit: śakunir uvāca na bhartuḥ śāsanaṃ vīrā raṇe kurvanty amarṣitāḥ alaṃ kroddhuṃ tathaiteṣāṃ nāyaṃ kāla upekṣitum
english: Śakuni said: "Heroes in their wrath heed not their lord's command in battle. Enough of being angered at them; this is no time to stand aloof.

sanskrit: yāmaḥ sarve 'tra saṃbhūya savājirathakuñjarāḥ paritrātuṃ maheṣvāsān madrarājapadānugān
english: "Let us all here join together, with our horse and chariots and elephants, and go to rescue those mighty bowmen, the followers of the Madra king.

sanskrit: anyonyaṃ parirakṣāmo yatnena mahatā nṛpa evaṃ sarve 'nusaṃcintya prayayur yatra sainikāḥ
english: "Let us guard one another with great effort, O king." So, all taking thought together, they set out to where the soldiers were.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca evam uktas tato rājā balena mahatā vṛtaḥ prayayau siṃhanādena kampayan vai vasuṃdharām
english: Saṃjaya said: Thus addressed, the king, encircled by a great host, advanced, making the earth tremble with his lion's roar.

sanskrit: hata vidhyata gṛhṇīta praharadhvaṃ nikṛntata ity āsīt tumulaḥ śabdas tava sainyasya bhārata
english: "Strike! Pierce! Seize! Smite! Cut them down!"—such was the tumultuous cry of your army, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: pāṇḍavās tu raṇe dṛṣṭvā madrarājapadānugān sahitān abhyavartanta gulmam āsthāya madhyamam
english: But the Pāṇḍavas, seeing in the battle the followers of the Madra king joined together, advanced upon them, taking up a central formation.

sanskrit: te muhūrtād raṇe vīrā hastāhastaṃ viśāṃ pate nihatāḥ pratyadṛśyanta madrarājapadānugāḥ
english: In a moment, O lord of peoples, those heroes, the followers of the Madra king, were seen slain in the battle, hand to hand.

sanskrit: tato naḥ saṃprayātānāṃ hatāmitrās tarasvinaḥ hṛṣṭāḥ kilakilāśabdam akurvan sahitāḥ pare
english: Then, as we pressed forward, the swift foe, their enemies slain, exultant and gathered together, raised shouts of triumph.

sanskrit: athotthitāni ruṇḍāni samadṛśyanta sarvaśaḥ papāta mahatī colkā madhyenādityamaṇḍalam
english: Then headless trunks were seen rising up on every side, and a great meteor fell straight through the disk of the sun.

sanskrit: rathair bhagnair yugākṣaiś ca nihataiś ca mahārathaiḥ aśvair nipatitaiś caiva saṃchannābhūd vasuṃdharā
english: With chariots shattered, with their yokes and axles broken, with great warriors slain, and with horses fallen, the earth was covered over.

sanskrit: vātāyamānais turagair yugāsaktais turaṃgamaiḥ adṛśyanta mahārāja yodhās tatra raṇājire
english: Borne along by horses swift as the wind, by steeds still fastened to their yokes, warriors were seen there, O great king, upon that field of battle.

sanskrit: bhagnacakrān rathān ke cid avahaṃs turagā raṇe rathārdhaṃ ke cid ādāya diśo daśa vibabhramuḥ tatra tatra ca dṛśyante yoktraiḥ śliṣṭāḥ sma vājinaḥ
english: In the battle some horses dragged chariots with broken wheels; some, bearing off half a car, wandered to the ten quarters; and here and there were seen steeds still tangled in their harness.

sanskrit: rathinaḥ patamānāś ca vyadṛśyanta narottama gaganāt pracyutāḥ siddhāḥ puṇyānām iva saṃkṣaye
english: And chariot-warriors were seen falling, O best of men, like Siddhas cast down from heaven at the exhaustion of their merits.

sanskrit: nihateṣu ca śūreṣu madrarājānugeṣu ca asmān āpatataś cāpi dṛṣṭvā pārthā mahārathāḥ
english: And when the heroes, the followers of the Madra king, had been slain, and the Pārthas, those great chariot-warriors, saw us bearing down upon them as well—

sanskrit: abhyavartanta vegena jayagṛdhrāḥ prahāriṇaḥ bāṇaśabdaravān kṛtvā vimiśrāñ śaṅkhanisvanaiḥ
english: —those smiters, greedy for victory, advanced with violence, raising the din of their arrows mingled with the blare of conches.
